summary: Submicron Al/AlO$_x$/Al/Ni$_{80}$Fe$_{20}$/Al tunnel ferromagnetic Josephson junctions have been fabricated using Manhattan-process lithography, achieving energy scales ($E_C \sim 40$ µeV, $E_J \sim 100$–130 µeV) compatible with transmon qubits. The junctions exhibit I-V characteristics and quantum phase diffusion signatures comparable to standard SIS junctions, with $C_J \sim 2$ fF and switching-current reduction of 70% consistent with WKB theory, establishing feasibility of ferrotransmon integration in standard superconducting circuits.
motivation: Ferrotransmons promise qubit frequency control via magnetic pulses rather than static fields, enabling scalable and energy-efficient cryogenic operation; however, submicrometer magnetic Josephson junctions have previously only been realized in Nb with focused ion beam processing, incompatible with standard circuit integration.
method: Three-step electron-beam lithography combined with angled Al evaporation, permalloy deposition, and in-situ oxidation produced SIsFS structures with layer thicknesses (Al 20/AlO$_x$ 2/Al 25/Ni$_{80}$Fe$_{20}$ 3/Al 70 nm); d.c. characterization was performed in a dilution refrigerator down to 10 mK with low-frequency current-bias measurements, and transport was analyzed using the tunnel junction microscopic (TJM) model and WKB simulations.
result: Stewart-McCumber parameter $\beta_C \approx 1$ and binding energy $E_B \sim 25$–40 µeV yield $E_C/E_J \sim 0.3$–0.4 and $E_B/E_J \sim 1$, placing devices in the quantum phase diffusion limit; measured subgap resistance $R_0 = 1.3$–3.9 kΩ agrees with WKB theory, and temperature dependence ($R_0$ saturation below 0.5 K where $E_B > k_B T$) confirms quantum origin of phase fluctuations.
